answer: Each identity claims one orchard row, locks an 80-credit bond on a terrace ledger, and gets a mirror copy published by a keeper. Each epoch it posts an orchard basket from that row, signed with its key. An auditor recomputes the terrace ledger against the mirror copy; a missing or reused basket, or a signature mismatch, burns the bond. The k-th fake identity pays 20 plus 2 times k minus 1: the 1,000th pays 2,018, and 1,000 fakes pay 1,019,000 plus 80,000 locked. A rented-row ring fails because a landlord key cannot sign a tenant harvest. An honest identity locks 80 once and pays one 20 fee.
